## ReadPage
Read the Browser's CURRENT page as an accessibility tree: every element as `- role "name" [refN] (states)`, indented by structure. Interactive elements (links, buttons, inputs…) get [refN] handles — pass that number as `ref` to Browser(click/type/hover). Refs are re-assigned on EVERY ReadPage call and go stale when the page navigates or re-renders — read again after you move.
• filter:"interactive" — only the clickable/typeable elements (flat list). Good default for acting.
• query:"…" — only lines containing the text (case-insensitive). Good for finding one control on a big page.
Reading the tree is exact and cheap — prefer it (and Eval) over screenshots for checking text/structure.

## Eval
Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the Browser's current page and return its value (JSON-serialized; promises are awaited — both top-level `await x` and an expression that returns a promise, e.g. `(async () => { …; return x; })()`). Use for exact checks a screenshot can't give: DOM assertions (`document.querySelector('.err')?.textContent`), computed styles (`getComputedStyle(el).color`), counts, extracting text/data, or poking app state. Multiple statements: wrap in an IIFE — `(() => { …; return x; })()`. Return JSON-serializable values (DOM nodes serialize as {} — return their properties instead). Use this for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION; to change app behavior, edit the source files. To fill in or click through a form, use ReadPage refs + Browser(click/type) — they send real input events; a scripted `el.click()` / `input.checked = true` often leaves Vue/React/Element-UI component state out of sync with the DOM (looks selected, submit still says the field is empty).

## Network
Inspect the network requests of the Browser's page (captured since the browser launched). Actions:
• list — recent requests as `[id] STATUS METHOD url (type, size)`; failed ones show the error. Filter with `filter` (substring of the URL, e.g. "/api") and `lines`.
• body — the response body of one request by `id` (from list). Text bodies returned verbatim (truncated); binary reported by size only.
Use it to verify frontend↔backend traffic: did the page call the endpoint, with what status, and what did the server actually return.

## Browser
Drive a real (headless) browser. This conversation has its OWN browser that persists across calls — the page you navigated to, clicked, and typed into stays put; ReadPage/Eval/Network operate on this same page. Other conversations running at the same time have their own tabs and viewport, so they never move your page (sub-agents you start share yours). Do not assume it is fresh: tabs you opened earlier in this conversation are still there. The user watches it live in dimensio's Browser panel and can take over. Site sign-ins are shared with the user's other conversations unless they turned on isolated storage for this one; sign-ins in the built-in browser persist across sessions and belong to the user: never sign out or change their credentials. Actions:
• navigate — go to a full http(s)/file URL, or a "/path" on the running Preview server; returns once the page has loaded and settled, and says whether the user can see the browser right now. Also: back | forward | reload.
• tabs — list open tabs (1-based index + title + URL; → marks the current one) and whether the user is watching.
• tab_new — open a NEW tab (optional `url`, default about:blank) and switch to it. Every tab keeps its own page state; all browser tools always act on the CURRENT tab.
• tab_switch — make another tab current (`tab`: 1-based index or targetId). Use it to work across pages — e.g. a reference site in one tab and your own app in another, switching to compare. Any other action also takes `tab` (switches first). When a click opens a popup / target=_blank link, the tool switches to the new tab and says so.
• tab_close — close a tab (`tab`, default = current). Closing the LAST tab closes this conversation's browser.
• attach — retarget this conversation's browser tools (this one plus ReadPage/Eval/Network) at an ALREADY-RUNNING Chromium-based app that exposes a DevTools port: an Electron desktop app or packaged exe launched with --remote-debugging-port=<port>, or any headful Chrome. Pass `port`; optional target:"substring" picks a window by title/URL when several exist. close then DETACHES without quitting the app.
• The USER'S OWN logged-in Edge / Chrome is not this tool: use DeviceBrowser with browser:<id|name> (Web Bridge, on their computer) — DeviceBrowser(action:"browsers") lists the browsers connected there.
• click — click by `ref` (from ReadPage / find — most reliable), by visible `text`, or by `x`/`y` (pixels of the last screenshot). Optional: button:"right", double:true, modifiers:"ctrl"|"shift"|…, force:true (click a covered ref anyway).
• type — focus a target (`ref` or CSS `selector`; omit to use current focus) and type `text` into it; the field is read back.
• key — press a key or combo: enter, tab, escape, backspace, delete, space, arrow keys, pageup/pagedown/home/end, or combos like "ctrl+a".
• scroll — scroll by `dy` (down) and/or `dx` (right) px, over `ref` or x,y (inner scroll areas, carousels); ref alone = scroll that element into view.
• hover — move the mouse over `ref` or `x`/`y` (reveals menus/tooltips).
• long_press (ref | x,y; ms, default 800) — press and hold; in touch mode the browser's own gesture pipeline fires contextmenu like a phone. drag (from ref | x,y → to_ref | to_x,to_y; ms = hold before moving) — moves in small steps; HTML5 drag-and-drop (draggable / links / images) is delivered as real drag events. pinch (x?,y?, scale) — two-finger zoom, touch mode only.
• set_value (ref | selector, value) — set a form control directly: native <select> (its popup is invisible in screenshots and cannot be clicked), checkbox / radio, date / time / range / color / number / text inputs, textarea, contenteditable — fires input + change; the control is read back.
• upload (files[], ref? | selector?) — put local files (absolute paths) into an <input type=file> (hidden inputs too; default = the first file input in the visible part of the page), then submit the form normally.
• find (text) — locate elements: every word must appear in the accessibility line; up to 20 lines with fresh [refN] handles — cheaper than paging ReadPage.
• page_text (maxChars?) — the readable text of the page (article / main first, else body) — far cheaper than ReadPage for articles, docs and long lists.
• resize — viewport: preset "mobile"|"tablet"|"desktop" or explicit `width`+`height` (mobile/tablet also emulate touch: touch events, mobile UA, pointer:coarse); optional colorScheme:"dark"|"light" to test themes. The default viewport is desktop (1280×900) — when the task is a MOBILE app/page, resize to preset:"mobile" FIRST and keep working there, so every screenshot and the user's live Browser pane show the phone-shaped layout, not a desktop letterbox. Re-screenshot before using coordinates.
• dprprobe — reload the current page at an emulated devicePixelRatio (default 2), scroll through it with real input, and check every <canvas> backing store for DPR-scaling bugs (feedback loops, blowout, runaway page height), then restore DPR 1. Headless default is DPR 1 — the one ratio where such bugs are symptom-free — while real displays run 1.25–3, so canvas/WebGL pages MUST pass this probe once after edits before being declared done. Counts as verification evidence.
• console — browser-side signals of THIS browser (console.*, uncaught errors, failed requests, auto-answered dialogs); query / errors_only filter. CDP-native: works regardless of any preview pane.
• screenshot — capture the CURRENT state. It first waits for running CSS/JS animations and web fonts to finish (up to 3 s); waitMs adds a fixed wait before that (e.g. for data to load), waitMs:0 captures immediately. Shoot ONE element with `selector` (CSS) or `ref` (from ReadPage) — scrolled into view if needed — or a rectangle with clip:{x,y,width,height}. A full-viewport screenshot becomes the coordinate basis for x,y. If you can see images it is handed back to you to judge; otherwise ask a specific `question` and a vision model returns a text verdict.
• wait_for — wait for expect:{…} to hold (or just ms) without acting.
• close — close this conversation's browser (all its tabs; a later action opens it again on a blank page).
Coordinates: x,y are pixels of the most recent screenshot image (the tool converts them to CSS pixels itself; full-viewport screenshots are 1:1 CSS px, scaled down only when the viewport is wider than 1568). A point outside that image is an error, not a silent miss.
Every click/type/key/scroll/hover/long_press/drag reports what actually happened: which element sat under the pointer and, after the page settles, URL/title change, focus moves, the clicked control's state (checked/expanded/selected/value), DOM changes, scrolling and new network requests; type reads the field back. "⚠ Nothing on the page changed" means it most likely missed — look before continuing. A ref whose element is covered by an overlay is refused (pass force:true to click anyway). type without ref/selector fails if nothing editable is focused.
expect:{text?, gone?, url?, selector?, focus?, value?, changed?} on any action waits (expect_timeout_ms, default 3000, max 15000) until all hold, else the action fails. wait_for(expect:{…}) waits for a condition without acting; wait_for(ms) just sleeps. verify:false skips the checks (faster, blind).
batch(actions:[{action,…}, …]) runs up to 20 steps in ONE call (same fields as single actions), stopping at the first failure — use it for predictable sequences like fill-and-submit. screenshot_after:true on any action appends a screenshot taken after the page settled.
Native alert/confirm/prompt dialogs are answered automatically so they never freeze the page (alert → OK, confirm/prompt → Cancel) and reported at the end of your next result; to accept a confirm, first Eval window.confirm = () => true.
Typical loop: navigate → ReadPage / find → click/type (by ref) with expect → Eval to assert DOM state → screenshot to verify visually. Prefer Eval/ReadPage assertions over screenshots for functional checks — cheaper and exact.
